newsitem.title: USA: Calif. to open intrastate gas lines to competition.
newsitem.headline: Calif. to open intrastate gas lines to competition.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission said Friday it approved an historic change in California's natural gas marketplace that will enhance competition and customer choice and is expected to result in lower prices for consumers.
It also establishes California as a national leader in the move toward deregulating gas distribution services and making them more competitive.
By a unanimous vote, the commission endorsed a comprehensive plan to restructure the way natural gas is bought, sold and transported in the state.

The plan, called the Gas Accord, is a collaborative settlement by Pacific Gas and Electric Co, a unit of PG&E Corp, and more than 25 gas industry participants and government and regulatory agencies. The Gas Accord will:
-- Increase the opportunity for all residential customers to pick the gas supplier of their choice, rather than purchasing gas exclusively from PG&E.

-- Change the pricing and regulatory structure for transporting natural gas within California and offer more transportation services and choices to natural gas customers. This is expected to result in lower natural gas prices with significant savings for customers over the next five years.

-- Resolve every major regulatory gas proceeding in which PG&E and other parties are involved to establish a foundation where the new market can operate efficiently. PG&E will make financial concessions of almost $300 million, enabling all parties to move forward into a competitive market without the burden of further litigation.

"This is a landmark step to further deregulate the natural gas industry here in California," said Jack Jenkins-Stark, senior vice president of PG&E. "These changes parallel those in the electric industry. Our customers will now have more energy choices, more services and lower prices."
